spec.title: Due Diligence Summary – Financial Health and Valuation Assessment of Meridian Clinical Supplies, Inc.
spec.subtitle: Ref: DD-27-1897706 | Date: 18 September 2026 | Prepared for: NorthBridge Capital Partners

sections.heading: Normalized Earnings and Historical Performance
sections.body: Meridian Clinical Supplies, Inc. generated FY2025 revenue of $182.4 million, representing a 6.8% CAGR over the prior three fiscal years. Reported EBITDA of $21.7 million includes approximately $3.4 million of non-recurring restructuring expenses, $1.1 million in one-time ERP implementation costs, and $0.9 million in excess owner compensation. After adjustments, normalized EBITDA is estimated at $27.1 million (14.9% margin). Working capital intensity averages 18% of revenue, with seasonal peaks in Q3 driven by hospital procurement cycles.

sections.heading: Financial Position and Cash Flow Quality
sections.body: As of 30 June 2026, the Company held $6.3 million in cash against $38.5 million in senior secured term debt, resulting in net leverage of approximately 1.2x normalized EBITDA. Free cash flow conversion has averaged 78% of adjusted EBITDA over the past three years, reflecting moderate capital expenditure requirements of roughly $4.2 million annually. Accounts receivable days stand at 61, slightly above the industry median of 54, primarily due to concentration in three large hospital systems. No material covenant breaches were identified under the existing credit agreement.

sections.heading: Legal and Operational Risk Assessment
sections.body: The Company is subject to two pending product liability claims relating to sterilization defects in a discontinued catheter line; outside counsel estimates a probable settlement range of $2.0–$3.5 million, which has not been fully reserved. Additionally, an ongoing FDA inspection cited documentation deficiencies in one manufacturing facility, requiring an estimated $1.8 million remediation investment over the next 12 months. Supply chain risk is moderately elevated due to single-source dependence on a Malaysian component supplier accounting for 27% of cost of goods sold. Management has initiated dual-sourcing efforts but has not yet secured alternative contracts.

sections.heading: Synergy Opportunities for NorthBridge
sections.body: NorthBridge’s existing portfolio company, Allied MedTech Distribution, operates a complementary sales network that could integrate Meridian’s product line within 9–12 months post-close. Revenue synergies are conservatively projected at $6.5–$8.0 million annually by Year 3 through cross-selling and expanded GPO contracts. Cost synergies of approximately $3.2 million per annum are achievable through consolidation of back-office functions, procurement leverage, and warehouse rationalization. Integration costs are estimated at $2.7 million, primarily related to IT harmonization and severance.

sections.heading: Valuation Range and Recommended Deal Protections
sections.body: Applying a market multiple range of 7.5x–8.5x to normalized EBITDA of $27.1 million implies an enterprise value between $203 million and $230 million. After deducting net debt and adjusting for the mid-point of estimated legal exposures, the implied equity value range is $161 million to $185 million. We recommend structuring $10–$15 million of the purchase price as an escrow or contingent value right tied to resolution of the pending litigation and FDA remediation milestones. Subject to satisfactory confirmatory diligence, a defensible offer would fall near the lower half of the range to reflect identified operational risks while preserving upside from synergy capture.

structure.full_text:
Due Diligence Summary – Financial Health and Valuation Assessment of Meridian Clinical Supplies, Inc.
Ref: DD-27-1897706 | Date: 18 September 2026 | Prepared for: NorthBridge Capital Partners

Section Normalized Earnings and Historical Performance
Meridian Clinical Supplies, Inc. generated FY2025 revenue of $182.4 million, representing a 6.8% CAGR over the prior three fiscal years. Reported EBITDA of $21.7 million includes approximately $3.4 million of non-recurring restructuring expenses, $1.1 million in one-time ERP implementation costs, and $0.9 million in excess owner compensation. After adjustments, normalized EBITDA is estimated at $27.1 million (14.9% margin). Working capital intensity averages 18% of revenue, with seasonal peaks in Q3 driven by hospital procurement cycles.

Section Financial Position and Cash Flow Quality
As of 30 June 2026, the Company held $6.3 million in cash against $38.5 million in senior secured term debt, resulting in net leverage of approximately 1.2x normalized EBITDA. Free cash flow conversion has averaged 78% of adjusted EBITDA over the past three years, reflecting moderate capital expenditure requirements of roughly $4.2 million annually. Accounts receivable days stand at 61, slightly above the industry median of 54, primarily due to concentration in three large hospital systems. No material covenant breaches were identified under the existing credit agreement.

Section Legal and Operational Risk Assessment
The Company is subject to two pending product liability claims relating to sterilization defects in a discontinued catheter line; outside counsel estimates a probable settlement range of $2.0–$3.5 million, which has not been fully reserved. Additionally, an ongoing FDA inspection cited documentation deficiencies in one manufacturing facility, requiring an estimated $1.8 million remediation investment over the next 12 months. Supply chain risk is moderately elevated due to single-source dependence on a Malaysian component supplier accounting for 27% of cost of goods sold. Management has initiated dual-sourcing efforts but has not yet secured alternative contracts.

Section Synergy Opportunities for NorthBridge
NorthBridge’s existing portfolio company, Allied MedTech Distribution, operates a complementary sales network that could integrate Meridian’s product line within 9–12 months post-close. Revenue synergies are conservatively projected at $6.5–$8.0 million annually by Year 3 through cross-selling and expanded GPO contracts. Cost synergies of approximately $3.2 million per annum are achievable through consolidation of back-office functions, procurement leverage, and warehouse rationalization. Integration costs are estimated at $2.7 million, primarily related to IT harmonization and severance.

Section Valuation Range and Recommended Deal Protections
Applying a market multiple range of 7.5x–8.5x to normalized EBITDA of $27.1 million implies an enterprise value between $203 million and $230 million. After deducting net debt and adjusting for the mid-point of estimated legal exposures, the implied equity value range is $161 million to $185 million. We recommend structuring $10–$15 million of the purchase price as an escrow or contingent value right tied to resolution of the pending litigation and FDA remediation milestones. Subject to satisfactory confirmatory diligence, a defensible offer would fall near the lower half of the range to reflect identified operational risks while preserving upside from synergy capture.

structure.heading: Financial Quality of Earnings and Liquidity Assessment (FY2022–FY2024)
text_content: **Financial Quality of Earnings and Liquidity Assessment (FY2022–FY2024)**

FY2024 revenue was $420.0M and Adjusted EBITDA was $58.0M, implying an Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 13.8%. Management-reported adjustments include restructuring charges, non-recurring legal settlements, and inventory write-downs; after normalizing for these items, core operating profitability appears stable. Audit reconciliations indicate limited aggressive recognition issues, though accrual policies for warranty reserves warrant targeted testing by acquirers.

Net debt as of 31-12-2024 was $120.0M, producing a net leverage ratio near 2.07x on a trailing twelve-month basis. Interest coverage remains adequate under current rates, but sensitivity testing shows covenant pressure if Adjusted EBITDA declines by 15% or if rates rise materially. The balance sheet supports targeted capex and integration spend, though refinancing timing through 2026 should be monitored. Covenant baskets remain available.

31) free cash flow was $22.0M, representing a cash conversion ratio of approximately 38% of Adjusted EBITDA. Free cash flow supports near-term liquidity but highlights limited cushion for dividend increases. Working capital cycling and seasonality require closer forecasting; recommended actions include: 1) tighten receivables DSO by 10 days, and 2) maintain a minimum liquidity buffer equal to three months of cash burn.

structure.heading: Legal Exposure, Operational Risk, Synergy Case, and Recommended Valuation Range
text_content: **Legal Exposure, Operational Risk, Synegry Case, and Recommended Valuation Range**

As of 202-503-15, the Company had three open litigations with a combined estimated exposure of $18.5M. These matters include contractual disputes with suppliers and a pending employment-related claim; management has recorded accruals aligned with outside counsel opinions and anticipates partial recovery under existing insurance, subject to deductibles and coverage limits. The outstanding cases are material to representations and warranties negotiations and may necessitate specific indemnities or escrows in the pruchase agreement. We recommend ongoing legal diligence to validate reserves, assess settlement probabilities, and quantify potential escrow sizing.

Operational risk is elevated by customer concentration: the top-3 custmoers represented 41% of FY2024 revenue, creating heightened renewal, pricing, and receivables exposure. Contract analysis shows shortre-term renewals and limited notice periods for two major accounts, increasing churn sensitivity during integration. Integration planning should prioritize dedicated retention teams, contract amendments where feasible, and strengthening credit controls. Financial modeling stress tests indicate a 10–20% attrition among those top accounts would materially compress Adjusted EBITDA and working capital headroom in the first 12–18 months post-close.

The synergy case supports a mid-to-high valuation outcome through defined cost and revenue initiatives. Cost synergies (G&A cnosolidation, headcount rationalization, and procurement optimization) are expected within 12–24 months; revenue synergies from cross-selling and channel expansion should phase in over 24–36 months. Using FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA of $58.0M as the baseline, the recommended enterprise value range is $480M–$620M (8.0x–10.5x). Valuation at or above the midpoint depends on timely integration execution and realization of identified synergies within 24 months, and due diligence will refine timing and deliverables.
